3	Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.
4	
5	- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. 7	- Expired Sitara deals cause bridgeback errors, allocation exceptions and feedback errors. Each one starts an email chain asking Daren to extend the deal or create a new one, often to cover tiny spillover volumes (0.3 to 24 dec). Volume Management then sets up a manual accounting arrangement, or parks the gas on stranger's gas.: This is the most common thread in the batch. Each case passes through 3 to 5 people (allocator → logistics → Daren → back), with deadlines tied to close. Aimee states that an accounting arrangement 'is always created every month' for meter 7266 and for the Cilco withdrawal, and Volume Management wants a deal so it doesn't have to make one every month. Possible fixes: evergreen or auto-roll rules, a tolerance for small overflow volumes, and an automatic expiry report before month end. # Leads

Work that readers of every message in the archive noticed, batch by batch, with the files that show it. None of it has been checked.

- Calpine emails a Word-document daily gas nomination to the HPL scheduler (cc Daren Farmer and others), often after a phone call covering the same thing. An HPL scheduler then confirms it by email.: The same attachment arrives almost every day from Dec 1999 to Apr 2001, and the person receiving it changes as staff turn over (Lloyd, Hadix, Lannou, Kemp). Messages say 'as we spoke of by phone', so the nomination is given twice, by phone and email. A monthly Calpine nomination and a revised resend also appear. Giron's reply ('Same volumes as yesterday, no changes') shows a manual confirm loop that could be an electronic nomination or an exception-only process. Attached please find the Hours Survey and Instructions for the month of May, 
2000.

I am sending the survey out this time as an opportunity to introduce myself 
to those of you I have not yet met.  I am being asked to take a direct roll 
in the further development and rollout of the Operations Pricing Model (fka 
Transaction Cost Model).  In the past, I have directed the implementation of 
several pricing systems based on activity based costing similar to the 
Operations Pricing Model (OPM).  Over the past couple of weeks my 
observations of the Model have lead me to be concerned with the quality of 
data used in the model.  It will take efforts by both you and the OPM team to 
get to a satisfactory level of data quality.  This process can start with 
this months data collection efforts.  Please pay particular attention this 
month as the "bar is being raised" by the management of Energy Operations for 
data quality and timeliness.

While completing the survey, take this time to review last month's numbers. 
Please return these surveys to Shari Mao by end of day Friday, June 2.  

Please note the following changes:
The Nat Gas RC's will now see deal validation and transportation rate 
activities therefore, these surveys will be notably longer but will not 
necessarily take more time

If the survey does not contain an activity that your team spends time on, 
PLEASE DO NOT TYPE ANY ACTIVITIES IN THE SURVEY.  Contact Jennifer Reside at 
#35971 to discuss how to proceed.

If you have any questions relating to the model or this survey, or are unable 
to meet the survey due date, please call Jennifer Reside at #35971 (Shari is 
on vacation this week).

input.prompt:
Proposal: Pre-fill the monthly Operations Pricing Model (OPM) Hours Survey and replace the Activity Driver Survey with standard system reports.

TODAY: Every month the OPM team (Shari Mao, Jennifer Reside, James Scribner) emails ~50 Energy Operations managers an Excel "Hours" survey, and ~24 managers a separate "activity driver" survey, then chases non-responders.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/997.eml (Shari Mao, 31 Mar 2000, "March Surveys", ~42 recipients): "please provide a completed \"Hours\" survey for each position within your group." and "If you're filling out the survey for your team, save a file for each of the positions you fill out for your team prior to filling out the next position. If you do not, the information will be lost."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1243.eml (June Hourly Survey, ~49 To recipients): "If your hours have not changed from last month, please send us an email to indicate so." — i.e. much of the answer is a repeat of last month.
- Driver survey: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/998.eml (March, 23 recipients), 856.eml (February), 1084.eml (April), 1154.eml/1180.eml (May), 1244.eml (June). Each says the survey is monthly and the sender herself offers the fix: 1084.eml "If your group currently generates a standard report that captures the surveyed data, please send the report to me, and put me on your recipient list beginning next month. This will eliminate your need to fill out this survey every month."
- Where it stalls: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1188.eml (Brenda Herod, 7 Jun 2000): "The deadline was Friday, 6/2, and unfortunately, very few of you responded. I understand how busy each of you are and you have expressed your concerns on the process burdening you." Missing surveys block cost allocation: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/923.eml (Shari Mao): "we have not received a survey from this person. This lack of information prevents your expenses from being 100% allocated out to the commercial teams."
- The survey later moved to Access (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1415.eml, 19 Sep 2000, ~57 recipients plus ~17 cc'd assistants) but stays a monthly manual fill-in.

CHANGE: (1) Hours survey is generated pre-filled with last month's hours per position (positions already come from the Org Database / ATEs, per 997.eml and 923.eml); managers only edit exceptions, and no reply = confirm. (2) For drivers, the OPM team subscribes to existing standard reports (deal counts, etc.) and pulls quantities automatically, as 1084.eml itself proposes; only RCs without a report still get a survey.

AFTER: Managers spend a few minutes confirming/adjusting a pre-filled form; most driver surveys vanish; OPM chasing drops.

ESTIMATE (monthly, the mail states the cadence is monthly):
- Hours survey: ~50 managers × (30 min today → 10 min) = 20 min × 50 = 1,000 min.
- Driver survey: ~24 managers × 15 min saved (assume half to two-thirds have a report; net of ~2 min OPM extraction) ≈ 360 min.
- OPM chasing/reminders (923.eml, 1188.eml): ~2 h saved = 120 min.
Total ≈ 1,480 min ≈ 24.7 h/month × $85 ≈ $2,100/month. No work is shifted: the pre-fill and report pulls are automated; extraction time is netted out.

No prompt-injection content seen in these files.

36	
37	Hello,
38	
39	We have prepared January and February data and will be scheduling meetings 
40	with you in the next few weeks.  For the month of March, please provide a 
41	completed "Hours" survey for each position within your group.  This survey 
42	will collect the  time your team spent on performing their activities in the 
43	month of March.   
44	
45	NOTE: We are now collecting EOL related activities.  If you spend time 
46	directly supporting EOL, and your survey does not have an activity that you 
47	can assign these times to, please contact me as soon as possible so we can 
48	add the appropriate activities to your survey.
49	
50	To fill out the survey:
51	
52	At the top of the spreadsheet, you will see a box labelled "Select Your RC".  
53	Click on the box and input your RC number, which will need to be 4 digits.
54	Once you have done this, another box will appear with the message "Select 
55	Position from Drop Box!" You can then select the position (i.e., staff, 
56	specialist, etc.) and "OK". The choices for positions are based on 
57	information contained in the Org Database (i.e., if a position is not listed 
58	that should be, please call me to discuss as it would indicate that 
59	corrections need to be made to the database).  Once you have the list of 
60	activities, please input hours (for the entire month) for each activity 
61	listed in the column labelled "Hours".
62	If you're filling out the survey for your team, save a file for each of the 
63	positions you fill out for your team prior to filling out the next position.  
64	If you do not, the information will be lost.
65	
66	We have included February compiled hours per position (if you had two 
67	specialists performing the same activity - 20 hours each, the "Last Month" 
68	column would show a total of 40 hrs for that month).  As with last month, you 
69	have the option to complete the survey on behalf of your entire group or send 
70	this survey to each of your team members, allowing each individual to fill 
71	out the time they spent on each activity.  If there are any activities you 
72	perform not included in your survey, please contact me as soon as possible 
73	for a copy of the Activity Dictionary.
74	
75	Please return these surveys by end of day Wednesday, April 5th.  If this is a 
76	problem, please notify me or Lisa Cousino immediately.
77	
78	Thanks,
79	Shari

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The problem is the idea itself, not how it was written up: the mail shows that both parts of the change were already in place by mid-2000.

**What's wrong:**

1. **The Hours survey already showed last month's hours.** In 997.eml (March 2000) Shari Mao wrote: "We have included February compiled hours per position ... the 'Last Month' column would show a total of 40 hrs for that month." Managers were already editing against last month's figures.
2. **"No reply means confirm" already nearly existed.** The proposal quotes 1243.eml itself: "If your hours have not changed from last month, please send us an email to indicate so." For an unchanged team, that's a one-line email. So the saving from pre-filling is close to zero, not the claimed 20 minutes for each of about 50 managers.
3. **The driver-survey fix was already on offer every month.** 1084.eml (April) and 1244.eml (June) both ask groups that have a standard report to send it in instead of filling out the survey. The proposal presents this as a new change, but it is the current process. Groups that haven't taken it up probably don't have a suitable report, so counting 15 minutes saved for each of about 24 managers has no support.
4. **The tool was already redesigned.** In September 2000 (1415.eml) the OPM team moved the Hours survey to a menu-driven Microsoft Access form. That replaced the Excel steps the proposal criticises, such as saving a file per position.
5. **The chasing is real but doesn't fit the estimate.** 923.eml and 1188.eml do show late replies and missing surveys blocking cost allocation. But the proposal gives no reason why its change would cut the chasing, since the existing shortcuts didn't. The 2 hours a month is a guess.

**What could fix it:** Find mail showing what still costs managers time after these shortcuts existed and after the move to Access. For example: how many groups actually switched to sending reports, why others didn't, and any complaints or late replies about the Access survey from October 2000 on. A proposal aimed at that remaining gap could hold up.

Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.

Proposal: Stop the daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report by adding the desk's rebook staff to Credit's distribution list.

TODAY: Credit (Veronica Espinoza, Russell Diamond, others) emails a "Credit Report--<date>" every business day to a ~35-person list that includes desk lead Darron Giron but not the staff on his desk who actually rebook the TAGG deals. Giron forwards each report, with no comment added, to whoever does it (Carole Frank, later Ryan O'Rourke).
- corpus/giron-d/sent/189.eml (27 Feb 2001): Giron to Carole Frank, "Subject: Credit Report--2/27/01", body is only "---------------------- Forwarded by Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT on 02/27/2001 10:24 AM", original "From: Veronica Espinoza/ENRON@enronXgate on 02/27/2001 10:22 AM" to a list of ~35 that includes "Darron C Giron/HOU/ECT@ECT" but not Carole Frank. Same pattern in 10.eml (5/9/01), 100.eml (4/3/01), 174.eml (3/1/01), 210.eml (2/20/01), 251.eml (2/7/01), 267.eml (2/2/01), all "X-To: Carole Frank"; 53.eml (4/20/01) "X-To: Ryan O'Rourke".
- Frequency: the archive holds ~71 such forwards in giron-d/sent (Subjects "Credit Report--1/24/01" in 259.eml through "Credit Report--5/9/01" in 10.eml) — essentially every business day, consecutive dates e.g. 3/19, 3/20, 3/21, 3/22, 3/23, 3/26, 3/27, 3/28, 3/29, 3/30 (149, 144, 138, 129, 128, 121, 125, 119, 106, 104).
- Where it stalls: when Giron is away the actions sit. corpus/giron-d/sent/154.eml, sent 19 Mar 2001, forwarding the 3/12/01 report a week late: "I don't know if you got any of these while I was out." The report contains action items like "CMS Energy Corporation qW3331.1 Rebook to CMS Marketing, Services and Trading" and "Engage Energy Canada LP qW3304.1 Rebook from ENA to ECC (Under the ISDA)" — so a week's rebooks were delayed.

CHANGE: Ask Credit to add Carole Frank / the designated rebook person (or a desk group mailbox) to the Credit Report distribution list, so the report goes straight to the person who acts on it. Giron stays on the list for oversight.

AFTER: No daily forward; rebooks start when the report arrives, including when Giron is out of the office.

ESTIMATE: ~2 min per forward for Giron (open, forward, address) plus ~1 min for the recipient to spot and open the forward rather than the original = ~3 min × ~21 business days = ~63 min/month ≈ 1.05 h ≈ $89/month. No work moves to anyone else (Credit's one-time list edit is negligible). Small, but the evidence is direct and the fix is trivial; it also removes the vacation backlog shown in 154.eml.

No prompt-injection content seen in these files.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. The idea of batching small write-offs could be fine. The evidence doesn't support it: the work looks like a one-time cleanup, and most items are too large for the proposed threshold.

**1. The memos are a cleanup of old flow, not steady monthly work.** Every memo I checked is about gas that flowed one to two years before the memo was sent:
- 1499 (7 Nov 2000): flow on 1/5/99.
- 2024 (3 Jan 2001): 6/16/99.
- 2033 (8 Jan 2001): 8/1/99.
- 1961: 1/1/99 to 9/30/2000.
- 2012: November–December 1999.
- 1973: January–June 1999.
- 2027: October–November 1999.
- 2036, the most recent: September–October 2000.

The memos come in a burst between December 2000 and January 2001, and 1973 says "Volume Mgmt had previously requested a deal to cover these volumes from someone, but never received one." That reads as clearing an old backlog. Nothing shows new small items arriving each month, so "ongoing" and a rate of 8 a month are not supported.

**2. "Most are small" is false.** Only about five memos fall under the proposed 100 MMBtu threshold: 2005 (16), 2006 (15), 2014 (18), 2024 (10) and 2033 (9). Most of the rest are large and would still get their own memo under the proposal:
- 1499: 1,703 MMBtu.
- 1961: 13,043.
- 2012: 30,287.
- 1973: 66,833.
- 1988: 3,962.
- 2013: 1,613.
- 2017: 1,075.
- 2020: 36,085.

Several also had a deal expire nearby, which the proposal itself says should still go to individual review. Five small items in about nine weeks is roughly 2 a month, during the cleanup only. That saves about 2.5 hours in total, not 3.75 hours a month.

**3. Smaller inaccuracies:**
- 1973 was sent to Gary Lamphier, not Daren Farmer.
- 2027 asks only for a deal, not a write-off approval.
- 1468 (Fred Boas) is a single instance and isn't one of Clem's memos. It doesn't show that the accounting arrangement is set up for every meter.

**What could change the verdict:** Strangers Gas write-off memos sent after January 2001 (or found in other mailboxes) about recent flow, showing small items keep coming at a steady rate. That would support both the ongoing claim and the rate.

Files are in `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-1\`:
- Rejection: `proposals\strangers-gas-writeoff-batch-reject.json`
- Decisions log: `decisions.md`

Group,

I received a call from Warren McReynold at the BPA today.  Warren was concerned with the level of service that our group is providing.  Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour.  The group at BPA cannot close their accounting books and meet reliability performance measures without our information.  I am meeting with Warren on Tuesday.  Warren is inclined to recommend to BPA that we are incapable of this service because of our inconsistent performance.  Such a recommendation would severely limit Enron's ability to produce value for our service customers in the near term and would likely prevent us from attracting new customers.  I believe that we can provide Warren's group with the information that it needs with minimal impact to our trading.

Therefore: 

We must call Grays Harbor and Frontier at the top of EVERY hour.  Then we need to call BPA and communicate the ACTUAL energy generated, not an estimate.  Finally, sign off the hour in the services book.  Les has provided us with the needed information for each day. Reserves can only be used for the hour that we are in, than we must resupply the schedule from a different source by working with the BPA marketers. If you have a question regarding reserves or pulling a schedule--please call Les or me.

Group,

We are long for the 13th in California, 25 mws under ST-WBOM in NP-15 at $57.  

We are also long 22 mws under ST-CALI in NP-15.  ST-CALI is also short in the morning in SP-15.  They are short at around $30.  ST-CALI is providing us with a sheet detailing their positions for RT, we will now be providing them with a sheet each morning detailing their sales from the previous day.  Going forward, please put all the ST-CALI sales or length in the service sheet beneath our activity.

We are also short 10 mws to EWEB for HE 1-12, Willamette has a month long sale at $270 but needs to come down unexpectedly for maintenance.  We will backfill this and split any profit with Services.

Finally...

We must check out with BPA each hour for Frontier and GCPUD.  Please make the call right after you call EPE dispatchers (between 25 after and 35 after).  The new service sheets have a place for initials for the call each hour, please initial after making the call to BPA (ext. 2277).

ALSO...TIMBERS TOMORROW NIGHT!

  "name": "Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report",
  "today": "Credit (Veronica Espinoza, Russell Diamond) emails a 'Credit Report' every business day to a list of about 35 people. When he is away the reports are not passed on: on 19 March he forwarded the 12 March report a week late, saying he didn't know if she had received any while he was out. input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace the hourly phone "generator checkout" (Grays Harbor / Frontier → BPA) on the Portland Real Time desk with automatic metering/telemetry feeding BPA.

TODAY: Around the clock, a real-time trader must phone the generators at the top of every hour, then phone BPA with the actual MWh, then initial the services sheet. This is done even for prescheduled hours, and it already stalls: BPA complained about missed or inconsistent calls and threatened to recommend dropping Enron from the service.
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/357.eml (Bill Williams III to the 12-person real-time group, 27 Jul 2001): "Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour. The group at BPA cannot close their accounting books and meet reliability performance measures without our information." / "Warren is inclined to recommend to BPA that we are incapable of this service because of our inconsistent performance." / "We must call Grays Harbor and Frontier at the top of EVERY hour. Then we need to call BPA and communicate the ACTUAL energy generated, not an estimate. Finally, sign off the hour in the services book." / "If this process takes more than 5 minutes, please let me know." / "we need to do this even if the generator is prescheduled, and must to continue to do this until these generators are automatically metered."
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/356.eml: Kate Symes: "So, do you mean we have to call EVERY hour?"
- corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/506.eml (12 Jun 2001, earlier version of the same duty): "We must check out with BPA each hour for Frontier and GCPUD. Please make the call right after you call EPE dispatchers (between 25 after and 35 after). The new service sheets have a place for initials for the call each hour, please initial after making the call to BPA (ext. 2277)."

CHANGE: Put the generators on automatic metering (the end state 357.eml itself names: "until these generators are automatically metered"), with interval data sent electronically to BPA and to the services sheet. Traders then only handle exceptions (meter failure, reserve deployment).

AFTER: No hourly calls to the generator or to BPA and no initialing. BPA gets actuals every hour without depending on a trader's attention, which removes the service-level risk in 357.eml.

ESTIMATE: 24 hours × ~30.4 days ≈ 730 checkouts/month (the mail states the cadence: "EVERY hour"). Per checkout ≈ 4 min of trader time (call generator(s), call BPA, initial the sheet; 357.eml sets 5 min as the upper bound). Saved ≈ 730 × 4 = 2,920 min ≈ 48.7 h/month × $85 ≈ $4,140/month. Counts only Enron trader time (generator-side and BPA staff are external and not counted). The work is not passed to another person; the meter replaces it. The one-time cost of installing metering is not netted.

No prompt-injection content seen in these files.

29	I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the

33	database, but prevent the main form from opening automatically.  Next, the 
34	admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database 
35	Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you 
36	can use the database as normal.
37	
38	Just a quick explanation:
39	
40	This is standard procedure for Access databases.  WeaponX imports and deletes 
41	a lot of data on a daily basis.  When data is deleted, the space is not freed 
42	up that was used by the data.  Therefore, as time goes by, the database size 
43	grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted.

45	The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one

cc:  
Subject: WeaponX

I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the 
following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already).

Open the database while holding down on the shift key.  This will open the 
database, but prevent the main form from opening automatically.  Next, the 
admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database 
Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you 
can use the database as normal.

Just a quick explanation:

This is standard procedure for Access databases.  WeaponX imports and deletes 
a lot of data on a daily basis.  When data is deleted, the space is not freed 
up that was used by the data.  Therefore, as time goes by, the database size 
grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted.

The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one 
for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB.  You can see that we will save 
several GB if everyone begins compacting the databases on a regular basis.

Please note:  Even though this is standard Access procedure, I would 
recommend that the book admin save a copy of their existing WeaponX file 
prior to compacting for the first time.  Once the file is compacted and a 
daily run has been successful, they can delete the backup file.  It is not 
necessary for them to save a backup copy each time before compacting.  I am 
only recommending it for the first compact.

I don't anticipate any problems with this procedure.  As a matter of fact, 
Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily 
basis.  In addition Ann (West desk) ran a test for me with no problems.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Greg

22	
23	Group,
24	
25	I received a call from Warren McReynold at the BPA today.  Warren was concerned with the level of service that our group is providing.  Warren explained to me the necessity and importance of calling in and reporting the actual amount of energy generated by Grays Harbor and Frontier EVERY hour.  The group at BPA cannot close their accounting books and meet reliability performance measures without our information.  I am meeting with Warren on Tuesday.  Warren is inclined to recommend to BPA that we are incapable of this service because of our inconsistent performance.  Such a recommendation would severely limit Enron's ability to produce value for our service customers in the near term and would likely prevent us from attracting new customers.  I believe that we can provide Warren's group with the information that it needs with minimal impact to our trading.
26	
27	Therefore: 
28	
29	We must call Grays Harbor and Frontier at the top of EVERY hour.  Then we need to call BPA and communicate the ACTUAL energy generated, not an estimate. cc:  
Subject: WeaponX

I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the 
following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already).

Open the database while holding down on the shift key.  This will open the 
database, but prevent the main form from opening automatically.  Next, the 
admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database 
Utilities/Compact Database.  After the database has completed compacting, you 
can use the database as normal.

Just a quick explanation:

This is standard procedure for Access databases.  WeaponX imports and deletes 
a lot of data on a daily basis.  When data is deleted, the space is not freed 
up that was used by the data.  Therefore, as time goes by, the database size 
grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted.

The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one 
for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB.  You can see that we will save 
several GB if everyone begins compacting the databases on a regular basis.

Please note:  Even though this is standard Access procedure, I would 
recommend that the book admin save a copy of their existing WeaponX file 
prior to compacting for the first time.  Once the file is compacted and a 
daily run has been successful, they can delete the backup file.  It is not 
necessary for them to save a backup copy each time before compacting.  I am 
only recommending it for the first compact.

I don't anticipate any problems with this procedure.  As a matter of fact, 
Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily 
basis.  In addition Ann (West desk) ran a test for me with no problems.

Please let me know if you have any questions.

Greg

Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
14	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
15	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
16	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
17	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). 18	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
19	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
20	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. 21	- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. TODAY: WeaponX (a per-admin Access database used by gas book administrators) imports and deletes data daily, so it bloats. Greg Couch told the six desk heads to have every book admin compact it manually at least weekly, using a shift-key open and menu steps.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/596.eml (Greg Couch to Gossett, Etter, Kelly, Baumbach, Giron and Keiser, 13 Oct 2000, forwarded by Giron to Anne Bike): "I would like each of your book admins using WeaponX to begin using the following procedures at least once/week (if they aren't already)." / "Open the database while holding down on the shift key. ... Next, the admin should go to Access menu selections and choose Tools/Database Utilities/Compact Database." / "WeaponX imports and deletes a lot of data on a daily basis. When data is deleted, the space is not freed up ... the database size grows and grows and needs to be periodically compacted." / "The Texas WeaponX file that I compacted reduced from 520 MB to 30 MB and one for the west went from 400 MB to 12 MB." / "Crystal (East desk I believe) already compacts the database on a daily basis."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/585.eml (17 Oct 2000): Giron re-forwards the same procedure to Anne Bike: "Try this and see if it does any good."
- Related fragility: corpus/giron-d/inbox/128.eml (Ryan O'Rourke, 11 Jan 2002): "A healthy, functional Weapon X has been saved out in the O\Dropbox\Kam folder. Please save this to your own hard drive and help distribute it."

CHANGE: Set Access's built-in "Compact on Close" option in the WeaponX front end (one setting, distributed with the next copy of the file, as in 128.eml), or add a compact step to the nightly import macro. No admin has to remember or perform the step.

AFTER: The database stays small automatically and the weekly (for some, daily) manual compaction stops, along with the reminder and forwarding emails.

ESTIMATE: At least 6 desks are addressed in 596.eml, each with one or more admins; assume 6 admins. ~5 min per manual compaction (reopen with shift, run the utility, wait for 400-520 MB to compact, reopen normally) × weekly × 4.33 = ~130 min/month ≈ 2.2 h ≈ $184/month (more where admins compact daily, as Crystal does). Nothing is handed to another person; the one-time setting change is negligible.

content.text:
I saved the proposal at about **$49 a month**, not the $89 you estimated. It ranks 3rd of 4 in `decisions.md`, and nothing else there covers the same work.

**What I confirmed in the mail:**
- `giron-d/sent` holds 71 Credit Report forwards, dated 24 Jan 2001 to 9 May 2001. They arrive almost every business day.
- In 189.eml, Credit sent the report at 10:22 to a list of about 35 people. Giron was on it and Carole Frank was not. He forwarded it to her at 10:24 with nothing added.
- The other files you cited also go to Carole Frank, except 53.eml, which goes to Ryan O'Rourke.
- In 154.eml, Giron forwarded the 12 March report on 19 March with "I don't know if you got any of these while I was out." That report lists deals to rebook, so the delay you describe is real.

**What I changed from your estimate:**
- **Minutes:** I used 2 minutes per forward in total, not 3. Forwarding with no comment is about a minute, and the person receiving it loses little extra.
- **How often:** The pipeline counts the rate only from the forwards listed in the proposal. When I listed 16, it came to 3.75 times a month. So I listed all 71, which gives 17.5 times a month over the four months. That is a little under your 21 business days, because some days have no forward in the archive.

The result is 2 minutes × 17.5 times a month ≈ 0.58 hours ≈ $49.30 a month. The proposal also mentions that rebooks would no longer wait while Giron is away, but that delay isn't counted in the dollar figure.

So I listed all 71, which gives 17.5 times a month over the four months. That is a little under your 21 business days, because some days have no forward in the archive.

I rejected this proposal because another critic had already saved the same work. It's entry 1 in `decisions.md`, "Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA". That entry proposes the same change (automatic metering so hourly actuals reach BPA and the services sheet without a trader's calls), cites the same messages (357.eml and 506.eml, plus 335.eml) and is valued at $3,102.50 a month. The check tool also flagged that both of this proposal's occurrences were already counted there. The rejection is recorded in `decisions.md`.

**The idea and evidence:**
- **Quotes:** All of them match 357.eml, 356.eml and 506.eml exactly.
- **How often:** "At the top of EVERY hour" does mean 24 checkouts a day, about 730 a month.
- **The fix:** The manager himself names automatic metering as the point when the calls can stop.

**One correction if this comes back:** 4 minutes per checkout is on the high side. "If this process takes more than 5 minutes, please let me know" means he expects it to take less than 5 minutes, not that 5 is a typical time. My draft used 3 minutes, which gives 36.5 hours, or $3,102.50, a month. That's the same figure as the saved entry. At 4 minutes the proposal claimed about $4,140 a month.

More research won't change the verdict. The only way this adds anything is if it covered different work from the saved entry, such as other generators or a different desk.

Proposal: Give Confirmations a self-service, back-dated counterparty MTM report so Risk desks no longer run and redact mini-books for every counterparty audit request.

TODAY: Counterparties' auditors ask Enron for third-party MTM valuations. Confirmations (Joe Hunter, Ellen Wallumrod) cannot value deals, so each request is emailed to all the gas desk heads (5-6 people). Each head forwards it to a book admin, who runs a mini-book for the counterparty as of a past date, blacks out Delta/Vol, exports it to Excel and emails it back.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/241.eml (Larry Joe Hunter to Wallumrod, Gossett, Keiser, Love, Giron, McLaughlin, Baumbach, 8 Feb 2001): "Until we can get EnTelligence built to our specifications, we'll need to continue to go to the different desks to provide Mark-to-Market valuations for a Counterparty's portfolio." / "please let these persons know that we will be coming to them often with these requests (we recieve several per week)." / "We do not have access to any system that values these deals, but are looking to get the on-line \"EnTelligence\" built so that it carries back-dated curves that will allow us to complete these requests without taking up a Risk person's time and without having to black out information (Delta/Vol) that is included in a mini-book." Giron's reply: "Call Pat Ryder for West desk requests."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/240.eml (9 Feb 2001), Hunter to 5 desk heads, forwarded by Giron to Patrick Ryder: "Please forward to Ellen Wallumrod the MTM valuation(mini-book) for all CoEnergy Trading Company deals as of Dec 31, 2000. If you can export into excel and forward by e-mail, that would be appreciated."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/214.eml (16 Feb 2001), to 6 desk heads, forwarded by Giron to Ryder: "Sorry for the late notice on this one. Can you provide MTM values as of Dec 29, 2000, for the short name of CROSS TIMBERS."

CHANGE: Build the tool the mail already names: a report (EnTelligence or a scheduled extract from the risk system) that keeps month-end curves and gives Confirmations MTM and open position by counterparty short name as of any past month-end, with Delta/Vol columns left out. Confirmations runs it directly.

AFTER: Confirmations answers each auditor request in a few minutes without contacting the desks. The broadcast to the desk heads, their forwards, the mini-book runs, the redaction and the Excel exports all stop.

ESTIMATE: Frequency from 241.eml, "several per week": assume 3/week ≈ 13/month. Per request today: Hunter's email ~3 min; 6 desk heads each read and forward or ignore it, ~2 min each = 12 min; the book admin(s) holding positions run the mini-book as of a past date, black out Delta/Vol, export and email, ~30 min; Confirmations receives and assembles, ~5 min. Total ≈ 50 min. After: Confirmations runs the report, ~10 min (this time is counted against the saving, since the work moves to Confirmations). Saved ≈ 40 min × 13 ≈ 520 min ≈ 8.7 h/month × $85 ≈ $740/month. Building EnTelligence is a one-time cost and is not netted.

Cites farmer-d/logistics/1005.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1018.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1021.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1023.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1029.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1041.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1043.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1158.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1168.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1274.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1286.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1308.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1372.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1386.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1406.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1458.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1479.eml, farmer-d/logistics/1982.eml, farmer-d/logistics/2003.eml, farmer-d/logistics/2023.eml, farmer-d/logistics/2077.eml, farmer-d/logistics/2113.eml, farmer-d/logistics/750.eml, farmer-d/logistics/755.eml, farmer-d/logistics/806.eml, farmer-d/logistics/872.eml, farmer-d/logistics/879.eml, farmer-d/logistics/881.eml, farmer-d/logistics/896.eml, farmer-d/logistics/898.eml, farmer-d/logistics/899.eml, farmer-d/logistics/995.eml

# Rejected

- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word nomination with a structured feed into HPL scheduling that rolls forward and is sent only when volumes change.. Why: The 16 minutes a day rest on steps the mail does not show: a phone call every day (only 5 of about 23 nominations mention one), HPL retyping the Word file (no message shows it), and frequent no-change days (none shown; REVISED resends and monthly nominations show volumes change), and the 30-a-month rate ignores that weekend days come in one Friday email (1330.eml); three critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the schedulers (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) showing what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as retyping it into the system, keying errors, corrections or rework after revisions, and nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller saving counted once per working day.
- Hourly generator checkout calls to BPA (Grays Harbor and Frontier): Meter the two generators automatically so their hourly output goes to BPA without a trader phoning it in.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA' ($3,102.50 a month), citing the same messages 357.eml and 506.eml.
- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only valuation view with back-dated curves so it can produce counterparties' audit MTM valuations itself, without going to the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off tiny Strangers Gas volumes under a standing approval and send the rest to Daren Farmer as one weekly electronic list instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 flows sent mostly in a burst from 11 Dec 2000 to 12 Jan 2001 and none appear after that, though the mailbox runs to late 2001; so the work is an episode that has ended, not 10 items a month, and the same work has already been rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, in this or other mailboxes (Cernosek, Lannou, Boas), that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.

9	# Rejected
10	
11	- Monthly OPM Hours and Activity Driver surveys: Pre-fill the Hours survey with last month's hours (no reply means confirm) and replace driver surveys with existing standard reports.. Why: The mail shows both parts of the change were already in place: the Hours survey already carried a 'Last Month' column, managers with unchanged hours could already just send an email, and every driver survey since April already invited groups to send a standard report instead, so the claimed 20 minutes saved per manager is not supported. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing what still takes managers' time after these options existed and after the September 2000 move to Access (for example, how many groups actually switched to sending reports, or complaints about the Access survey), and build the proposal on that remaining gap.
12	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey from last month, make the commercial-team split required, and take driver counts from standard reports instead of the spreadsheet.. Why: Two of the three changes already exist in the mail (FTE and commercial-team rollover, a prior-month hours report, and the standing offer to accept standard reports instead of the driver survey), and the 1,630 minutes a month rests on a padded headcount (the 50 on 2080.eml include cc'd directors and the OPM staff), a skipped-month frequency, and guessed per-person and chase figures. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing how many managers actually fill in the hours survey each month, how long it takes them, how many RCs took up the report option and why the others did not, and how often the OPM team has to chase missing commercial-team splits; a proposal limited to the required-split check, or to pre-filling the hours themselves, might hold up on that evidence.
13	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill each manager's hours survey from ATEs headcount and last month's split, and replace driver surveys with standard system reports, so managers only confirm changes.. Why: The mail shows most of the change was already in place (the Access hours survey rolled over FTEs and commercial teams and printed prior-month hours by activity, unchanged months needed only an email, and every driver survey already offered a standard report instead), so the minutes saved are not supported; two critics have already rejected the same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what still costs managers time in the Access survey after rollover existed, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, and how often OPM chases missing surveys; a proposal aimed only at that remaining gap (for example an automatic missing-survey list from ATEs) might hold up.
14	- Monthly OPM activity-driver and hours surveys: Pull activity-driver counts from system reports and pre-fill the hours survey with last month's figures so managers only confirm changes. Why: The mail shows the OPM team had already built most of this: from September 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that carries over commercial teams and headcount and shows last month's hours, and the activity-driver survey does not appear after August 2000, so the claimed 1,064 minutes a month are mostly not there to save. Research that could settle it: Look for activity-driver survey requests after August 2000 and for time spent on the Access hours survey after it carried data over (from March 2001 on); only the gap between showing last month's hours in a report and pre-filling them could still be saved, and that needs its own evidence.
15	- Monthly OPM hours and activity driver surveys: Pre-fill the OPM hours survey with last month's hours and Org Database/ATEs positions, take driver quantities from standard reports, and treat non-responders as carry-forward.. Why: Most of the change already exists in the mail (since the September 2000 Access survey, FTEs and commercial teams roll over and a prior-month hours report is built in; unchanged-hours managers could already just email; every driver survey already offered to accept a standard report), so the 'today' describes a retired spreadsheet process and the 915 minutes a month saved is unsupported; this is also the third proposal for the same work, already rejected twice in decisions.md. Research that could settle it: Find mail from after the Access rollout showing what still costs managers time, such as how long the survey takes, how many RCs actually switched to sending reports and why others did not, or how often OPM must chase missing surveys, and limit the proposal to that remaining gap.
16	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off Strangers Gas items under a size threshold automatically and have Daren Farmer sign one monthly batch report instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of old 1999-2000 flows sent in a burst from Dec 2000 to Jan 2001, not steady monthly work. Only about 5 of the roughly 20 memos are small enough for the threshold, so the claim that most are small and the rate of 8 small items a month are both wrong. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, or in other mailboxes, that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
17	- Monthly OPM hours and activity-driver surveys: Pre-fill the hours survey from last month and ATEs headcount, take driver counts from existing reports, and automate reminders.. Why: The proposal describes the June 2000 process as today's, but the mail shows it was replaced: from October 2000 the hours survey ran in an Access tool that rolls over commercial teams and FTE headcount and reports last month's hours (1415, 1436, 2015, 2080), every driver survey already offered a standard report instead (856 to 1244), and no driver survey appears after the July 2000 one (1319), so the 1,655 minutes a month are mostly not there to save; four critics have already rejected this same work for this reason. Research that could settle it: Find mail from 2001 on showing what still costs managers time in the Access hours survey once rollover worked (complaints, help calls, late returns), how many groups actually switched to sending reports, and any driver-survey requests after August 2000; only a proposal aimed at that remaining gap, such as pre-filling the hours themselves or an automatic list of missing surveys from ATEs, could hold up.
18	- Calpine daily gas nomination handling: Replace Calpine's emailed Word nomination, phone call and confirmation email with a structured nomination that rolls forward and needs a reply only when it changes.. Why: The mail shows only that Calpine emails a Word nomination on weekdays; the phone call on every day, the HPL confirmation loop, the re-keying and the daily-including-weekends rate are not supported, and the estimate counts Calpine's own time, so the 13 minutes a day is not realistic. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with the Calpine nomination: replies or confirmations sent to Calpine, keying errors or corrections, or revised nominations that caused rework. Evidence like that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the Enron scheduler.
19	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus Word-document nomination with a standing nomination in HPL's system that rolls forward and is changed only by exception through electronic entry.. Why: Most of the minutes claimed come from steps the mail does not show happening daily: a phone call (mentioned in 4 of about 23 nominations), a scheduler confirmation reply (one undated internal Giron-to-Poorman note, not a reply to Calpine), and frequent no-change days that would make a standing nomination worthwhile (no evidence; monthly totals and REVISED resends show the volumes change). Research that could settle it: Find scheduler replies to Ricky Archer's nominations, and nomination contents or comparisons that show how often Calpine's daily volumes actually repeat; also whether HPL had an electronic nomination entry Calpine could use.
20	- Gas flowed at a meter after the deal expired, or with no deal: Roll expired deals forward automatically, write off small volumes under a standing approval, and send the remaining items to the trader as one electronic batch list.. Why: The 20 items a month mostly come from Clem Cernosek's memos, a one-time burst of 1999-2000 flows sent from December 2000 to January 2001, and that same work has already been rejected; also, the memos are not small (2002.eml has 11,980 MMBtu, 1985.eml 2,164), rolling a deal forward 'at the same terms' goes against the trader's word that such deals must be renegotiated (1458.eml), and 804.eml does not show a six-month stall on an expired deal. Research that could settle it: Look for ongoing expired-deal or no-deal requests after January 2001 (Lannou, Young, Olsen, McCoy, Poorman and others) to show a steady monthly rate, and for traders extending deals unchanged, to show how many could safely roll forward; a proposal limited to batching the existing feedback-monitor list for one approval might hold up on that evidence.
21	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's daily phone call plus emailed Word nomination with one structured electronic nomination and a standing 'same as prior day' rule, so HPL acts only on changes.. Why: The 10 minutes a day saved rest on steps the mail does not show: a daily phone call (mentioned in only 4 of about 23 nominations, and 169.eml says 'will call if there are any changes'), no-change days (nothing shows volumes repeating, and REVISED resends, monthly totals of 79-85 and force-majeure claims show they change), and HPL re-keying the Word document (never shown); the 30-a-month rate also ignores that weekend nominations come in one Friday message (1330.eml), and two critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Look in the schedulers' own mailboxes (Robert Lloyd, Juliann Kemp) for what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as replies to Ricky Archer, keying errors or corrections, or rework caused by revisions, and for nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller weekday-only saving for the scheduler's keying step.
22	- Monthly flip of ECC third-party deals to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book: Book any deal where ECC is the Enron party with a third counterparty to FT-US/CAND-ERMS automatically in EOL and TAGG, plus a nightly exception report.. Why: The proposed rule keys on ECC being the Enron party, but the mail shows the deals that stall invoicing are booked as ENA with counterparties that hold ECC master swaps (Aquila Canada, Duke), and that EOL already auto-books by counterparty for TransCanada Energy and Dynegy Canada (giron-d/sent/292, 192, 108), so the change as written misses the main cause and ignores the fix that already exists, while the proposal cites four messages from Oct-Dec 2000 out of about twenty that run to March 2001. Research that could settle it: Rebuild the proposal on the full thread (giron-d/sent 108, 114, 164, 168, 192, 195, 246, 250, 270, 292, 406, 419, 459, 460, 535, 539 and the four cited): make the change extend the existing EOL counterparty programs to a maintained list of ECC master-swap counterparties, with TAGG flagging ENA deals with those names; check whether the Duke program was ever set up; and count the requests per month and the people on each to set the frequency and minutes.
23	- Back-dated MTM valuations for counterparties' auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only report of MTM value by counterparty and past date, across all regions and without Delta/Vol, so it can answer auditors without asking the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
24	- Calpine daily gas nomination to HPL scheduler: Replace Calpine's phone call plus emailed Word nomination with a structured feed into HPL scheduling that rolls forward and is sent only when volumes change.. Why: The 16 minutes a day rest on steps the mail does not show: a phone call every day (only 5 of about 23 nominations mention one), HPL retyping the Word file (no message shows it), and frequent no-change days (none shown; REVISED resends and monthly nominations show volumes change), and the 30-a-month rate ignores that weekend days come in one Friday email (1330.eml); three critics have already rejected this same work for these reasons. Research that could settle it: Find mail from the schedulers (Robert Lloyd, Susan Hadix, Aimee Lannou, Juliann Kemp) showing what HPL does with each Calpine nomination, such as retyping it into the system, keying errors, corrections or rework after revisions, and nomination contents showing how often volumes repeat; that could support a smaller saving counted once per working day.
25	- Hourly generator checkout calls to BPA (Grays Harbor and Frontier): Meter the two generators automatically so their hourly output goes to BPA without a trader phoning it in.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved as 'Hourly generator check-out calls to BPA' ($3,102.50 a month), citing the same messages 357.eml and 506.eml.
26	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a read-only valuation view with back-dated curves so it can produce counterparties' audit MTM valuations itself, without going to the risk desks.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2), which cites the same messages 214, 240 and 241 and makes essentially the same change.
27	- Strangers Gas write-off approval memos: Write off tiny Strangers Gas volumes under a standing approval and send the rest to Daren Farmer as one weekly electronic list instead of a paper memo per meter.. Why: The memos are a one-time cleanup of 1999-2000 flows sent mostly in a burst from 11 Dec 2000 to 12 Jan 2001 and none appear after that, though the mailbox runs to late 2001; so the work is an episode that has ended, not 10 items a month, and the same work has already been rejected in decisions.md for this reason. Research that could settle it: Look for Strangers Gas write-off memos about current-month flow after January 2001, in this or other mailboxes (Cernosek, Lannou, Boas), that show small items keep coming at a steady rate.
28	- Counterparty MTM valuations for auditors: Give Confirmations a counterparty valuation report with stored year-end and month-end curves, so they can answer audit requests without going to the desks.. Why: The same work and essentially the same change are already saved as 'Answering counterparty auditors' MTM valuation requests' (decisions.md item 2, $1,381.25 a month), which cites the same messages 137, 214, 240 and 241.
29	- Daily hand-forwarding of Credit's Credit Report: Put the book administrators who rebook the deals (Carole Frank and others) on Credit's Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 3, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards to Carole Frank in giron-d/sent.
30	- Flipping ECC master-swap deals out of Houston books: Have EOL/TAGG book deals with ECC's master-swap counterparties straight to the FT-US/CAND-ERMS book, with a daily exception report, instead of manual search-and-flip requests.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as item 3, 'Monthly search of Houston books for Enron Canada (ECC) deals', which cites the same Giron messages.
31	- Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report: Put the West desk's rebook handler (Carole Frank) or a desk mailbox directly on Credit's daily Credit Report list, so Darron Giron no longer forwards it every business day.. Why: This work and change are already saved as 'Daily hand-forwarding of the Credit Report' (decisions.md item 4, $49.30 a month), which cites the same 71 Giron forwards in giron-d/sent.

content.text:
I saved the proposal. It is number 4 of 6 in decisions.md, at **24 minutes a week, which comes to 1.73 hours or $147.05 a month**. Nothing else in decisions.md covers WeaponX or compacting.

**Checked against the mail:**
- In `giron-d/sent/596.eml`, Greg Couch asks six desk leads to have every book admin compact WeaponX by hand "at least once/week". That message has the shift-key steps, says the database "imports and deletes a lot of data on a daily basis", gives the 520→30 MB and 400→12 MB sizes, and says Crystal already compacts every day.
- `giron-d/sent/585.eml` is Giron forwarding the same memo to Anne Bike again on 17 Oct.
- In `giron-d/inbox/128.eml`, a new copy of the file was handed out through a shared Dropbox folder. That shows one copy with the setting turned on could reach everyone.

**What I changed before saving:**
- **Minutes:** I cut the saving from 5 minutes per admin to 4, so 6 admins × 4 = 24 minutes a week. Once the file is compacted every week it stays small (about 12–30 MB), so compacting it is quick. The 400–520 MB sizes the proposal used for its timing only applied to files that had never been compacted.
- **How often:** I used the memo's own "at least once/week" as the stated rate. The check used it because it is higher than the rate counted from the mail.
- **Wording:** "Nightly import macro" became "the daily run", since that is what the mail calls it. I also noted that "Compact on Close" exists only in Access 2000 and later.

**Weak points managers should know:**
- The only evidence is one instruction memo, sent in October 2000, and a forward of it. No message shows how many admins actually compact each week.
- The figure of six admins is an assumption: one per desk lead on the memo.
- The mail doesn't say which version of Access WeaponX runs on. If it is Access 97, "Compact on Close" doesn't exist, and the fallback is the compact step at the end of the daily run.

Kourtney
