Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Producer Services staff entering deals in Sitara themselves, and whether deal entry is kept with logistics or deal-entry staff as a control; then count the actual spot and interim tickets requested per month across the whole year.
- Producer Services wellhead purchase ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services keys spot and one-month wellhead purchase tickets into Sitara itself instead of emailing logistics to re-key them. Why: The proposal rests on Producer Services already entering committed-reserves tickets in Sitara, but the mail shows the opposite: they write those tickets up and ask for the Sitara number after someone else enters them (789.eml: "Please supply the sitara number once entered"; 694.eml: "We will generate a ticket to be entered into sitara ASAP"), so the change means giving deal-entry rights to a new group, which the mail gives no basis for, and the time saved is small and guessed. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services (Taylor, Smith, Reinhardt, Graves) entering deals in Sitara themselves, or saying why deal entry is held by logistics or deal capture (a control rule or system access), and for any statement of how long Tom Acton spends entering these tickets.
- Weekly check of ERMS curves against RisktRAC: A nightly automatic comparison of the ERMS and RisktRAC curve and book lists replaces the weekly manual review.. Why: The same work is already saved as 'Setting up new forward curves in RisktRAC and TAGG', which cites the same message (giron-d/sent/410.eml) and already replaces the weekly manual check with a nightly gap report.
- Transwestern marketers' weekly bullets round: Replace Kim Watson's Friday email request for bullets with a shared bullets page each account director fills in, with no 'none' replies.. Why: The mail shows only two bullets rounds in all (Fri 8 Mar and Fri 22 Mar 2002), Lokay sent other mail on Fridays 1 Mar and 15 Mar with no bullets, so the weekly rate of 4.3 a month is not supported, and the main time saved (Watson assembling the replies into a summary) does not appear in the mail at all. Research that could settle it: Look in Kimberly Watson's or the other account directors' (Lindberg, Lohman, McConnell, Y'barbo) mailboxes for further 'Bullets' requests and replies, and for the summary Watson builds from them, to show how often the round really happens and what she does with the replies.
- Emailing dated curve files to JPMorgan: Send the dated curve file to JPMorgan automatically from the official curve close, to a fixed address list, instead of Darron Giron emailing it by hand. Why: The mail shows only two such sends, six weeks apart, among the 163 messages Giron sent in Dec 2000 and Jan 2001, so the claimed every-business-day frequency is unsupported; several other claims about how the work is done are not in the mail either. Research that could settle it: Look for more Giron-to-JPMorgan curve emails, or any message saying JPMorgan gets curves on a schedule (daily, weekly, under a contract), and for anything showing the work takes minutes or causes errors beyond the one 'Sorry wrong address' resend.
- Manager approval of small expense reports in Concur: Auto-approve expense reports under $100 in Concur, with the manager reviewing a monthly digest afterwards.. Why: The five approvals in 12 days were a one-time rush to clear expenses before the group left Enron's expense system for UBSW Energy, so the work ends and the monthly rate of 12 is not real; the whole archive shows only seven such reports. Research that could settle it: Look for this approval work, and how often it happens, under UBSW Energy's new expense process after the transaction closes; Enron's Concur/XMS approvals for this group stop there.
- HL&P month-to-date flow report and shortfall check: Have the system produce the HL&P daily nominated-versus-flowed report, with the 5% tolerance and buyback volumes worked out, instead of a hand-built spreadsheet emailed each week.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 16, 'HL&P month-to-date flow report', which cites all eleven of these update emails plus the 12/99 shortfall thread (683.eml) and the June 2000 resend (1217.eml).
- Setting up a new trading book across TAGG, Sitara, RisktRAC/ERMS, CPR and EOL: One routed new-book request form with status tracking and a single completion notice, instead of separate emails to each system's administrator. Why: The routed process already exists: Shona Wilson's memo (giron-d/sent/410.eml, Nov 2000) says one RisktRAC book request form goes to Risk Analysis and Reporting, which forwards it to the ERMS administrator and Global Counterparty and sends a final email to the books list, and says this process had 'formally existed for a number of months'; Giron's own requests from Oct 2000 on (557, 564, 491, 160) are single form submissions to Trevino/McIntyre, so the scattered emails cited come from mid-2000, when people were not following the process, not from how the work runs now. Research that could settle it: Only a new angle could revive it: mail from after Nov 2000 showing that book requests made through the single form still bounce, stall or need follow-up emails to CPR, EOL or Sitara administrators. The steps the form does not cover (the CPR region and EOL trader mapping) would then be a narrower proposal, with its own count of how often it happens.
- Settling HPL day/spot deal price and volume disputes: Sitara sends each counterparty a next-morning recap of the prior day's HPL day deals so price and volume mismatches are fixed at once, not at invoicing.. Why: The disputes are a post-sale cleanup: HPL passed to AEP from June 2001 (136.eml, 106.eml 'a deal from when we were at Enron'), every disputed deal is for Dec 2000 to May 2001 production, the earlier mail shows only about three such threads in all of 2000, and several cited threads are not day-deal disputes, so there is no ongoing work at 5 a month for a recap to prevent. Research that could settle it: Find disputes over day deals in Enron's own books after June 2001, outside HPL (for example ENA Texas or other desks' settlements mail), at a steady rate, plus evidence of whether those deals were already confirmed by Enron's Confirmations group; without that the verdict stands.
- Upkeep of TW's second, unposted Current Shipper rate matrix: Ask the recipients once whether anyone uses the unposted matrix, and retire it if nobody does.. Why: The archive shows the second matrix being sent only once (29 Oct 2001), and no message says how often Current Shipper rates change, so there is no basis for how often the saving would happen. Research that could settle it: Look for other Current Shipper or Global Settlement rate changes, other TW rate matrix postings, or anything that gives a schedule for those changes (for example, in Rita Bianchi's, Elizabeth Brown's or Jeanette Doll's mail). Two or more dated sends, or a stated schedule, would give a rate.
- Building the daily El Paso Electric (EPE) preschedule/schedule sheet: Generate the daily EPE schedule sheet from e-tags and Enpower deals, check it automatically against EPE's dispatch, and phone only the counterparties on the exception list.. Why: The change depends on tag data the mail shows Enron does not get (52.eml: the missing tag did not list EPMIWE, and only EPE's dispatchers had it), the error rate of 8 days a month is about four times what the mail shows, the checkout-call part repeats work already rejected (decisions.md item 60), and 133.eml is a turbine-outage note, not a daily EPE file. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing Enron could read every tag in EPE's control area (for example as EPE's agent on the tagging system) and that the tags exist when the day-ahead sheet is built; count the schedule errors in the EPE sheet over several months; and find anything saying how long preschedule spends building the sheet each day.
- Month-end basis and index roll-off calculated twice: Have the risk system produce the 100% basis view and the rolled-off V@R view from one calculation, using a month-end roll-off percentage set centrally.. Why: The same work is already saved as item 3, 'Month-end basis and index roll-off in the gas risk books', which cites the same two messages (giron-d/sent/631.eml and 442.eml) and proposes the same change.
- Monthly vacation round and out-of-office coverage notices in Energy Operations / HPL logistics: One shared absence calendar replacing the monthly vacation request round, plus a standing desk-coverage matrix so out-of-office notices go only to backups. Why: The vacation-round half is already saved (decision 24, same calendar, same files 954/1143/1282), and the coverage-notice half rests on miscounted notices and a change that would stop telling the people who need to know who to call. Research that could settle it: A coverage-only proposal would need many more distinct scheduler out-of-office notices across the year, and something in the mail showing that callers went to the wrong person or that notices took real effort to write or re-send. Without that, the savings stay a few minutes a month.
- Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration report: Generate the report as a scheduled query from the Global Contracts database before each bid week and send it to a self-service subscription list.. Why: The same work is already saved in decisions.md as item 18, 'Monthly HPL Assignment, Termination & Expiration Report', with the same change and the same messages (farmer-d/logistics/211.eml, 2114.eml), so saving it again would count the saving twice.
- Monthly TECO Seven Oaks (meter 6884) under/over-take adjustment: Paper the adjustment with TECO and set up standing evergreen purchase and sale deals at meter 6884 so volume management stops asking the desk for deals each month. Why: The account of today's work is out of date: the mail shows standing buy/sell deals (purchase 137870, sale 235670) were set up at meter 6884 after June 2000, and the 2001 stalls come from those deals expiring at 12/00 and from TECO being replaced by El Paso as the counterparty, which an evergreen TECO deal would not fix; the monthly frequency and 42 minutes rest on one request and one remark. Research that could settle it: Restate the work as extending or re-booking the meter 6884 buy/sell deals when they expire or the counterparty changes (corpus/farmer-d/logistics/2093.eml, 2095.eml, 2099.eml, 2149.eml, 2150.eml, 95.eml), count how often that actually happens, and propose a change aimed at that, such as booking the deals for the full term of the lease or plant agreement and rolling them over when the counterparty changes.
- Seven Oaks / meter 6884 monthly tailgate adjustment deals: Paper the Seven Oaks adjustment with El Paso (formerly TECO) and book one standing buy/sell deal pair at meter 6884.. Why: The same work is already saved as decisions.md item 22 ('Seven Oaks meter 6884 monthly plant adjustment deals', standing evergreen purchase and sale with El Paso), citing the same files 1626, 194, 2067, 2099 and 95.
- Monthly RC allocation % update to commercial teams: Pre-fill each RC's monthly allocation % from the OPM hours survey's commercial-team split, so directors reply only if they disagree.. Why: The allocation file is already sent pre-filled with last month's or preliminary percentages and asks only for changes (862, 1083), and nothing in the mail shows the OPM survey produces per-RC commercial-team percentages that could replace it (1447 shows OPM itself still missing the split), so most of the 520 minutes are not there to save and rest on a guessed 70 managers. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing that OPM's Access tool actually holds hours by commercial team for each RC, on the same team list and month as the Consolidations file, and replies to the allocation file showing how many directors and managers actually change percentages each month and how long it takes them.
- Annual budget staffing and salary worksheet: Pre-fill each manager's budget staffing and salary worksheet from an HR/payroll extract by RC. Why: The mail contradicts the estimate: Diane asks managers for only 'a little bit of information', the salary step is a short list of positions with a one-word high/low guess, and she says averages are as accurate as current salaries, so a payroll pre-fill would remove only a few minutes per manager once a year, not 30. Research that could settle it: Look for mail from later budget cycles (2001 for 2002) or from managers showing that the salary and roster step actually took them substantial time, needed several exchanges with Diane, or produced budget errors.
- Monthly Investor Relations volumetric variance explanations: Have the monthly Statistical Database refresh list the top counterparty and EOL/non-EOL drivers for each region with a >10% variance, so controllers confirm drivers instead of researching them.. Why: decisions.md has already rejected this work twice for the same gaps, and this version repeats them: nothing in the mail shows that the Statistical Database holds counterparty or EOL detail, or that controllers research drivers by hand (Baumbach's one- and three-line replies name the drivers from memory, the August one the next morning), and the 20-to-8-minute saving for 11 controllers is costed from one controller's replies. Research that could settle it: Find mail showing what the Statistical Database contains (counterparty or EOL breakdowns), replies from controllers other than Baumbach, and requests for other months, showing that working out the drivers takes real lookup time; then cost only that lookup step for the controllers who actually reply.
- Double booking of PG&E Texas transport on ENA and an ENA-HPL desk-to-desk deal: Have Legal transfer the ENA PG&E Texas transport contracts to HPL and drop the ENA-HPL desk-to-desk deal, so the transport is scheduled and allocated once.. Why: The organization later decided against the change: in April 2001, as HPL was being sold to AEP, Daren Farmer wrote that the PGEV transport contracts should stay with ENA (farmer-d/logistics/155.eml), and the only evidence for the work is one April 2000 memo that gives no frequency.

I have re-checked Sitara & verified that the above deal was a Term, Firm deal.  This resulted in a GTC Purchase Firm contract being set-up in the Global Contracts System.  The term of the GTC was set as the term of the deal (4/1/00 thru 3/31/01) with no evergreen, meaning that the contract will expire at the end of this month.

To the best of my knowledge, all GTC Purchase Firms have the same language & they do not have evergreen.  They expire at the end of the primary term.

So, unless Exxon negotiated a deal with different, special language to allow for evergreen & included something about a "10 day notification" to terminate, there isn't any reason to "terminate" this contract.

If this is the case, please advise.  Otherwise, I don't think we need to do anything.  The contract will expire at the end of this month on its own.






Elsa Villarreal

Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
X-From: Mary Poorman
X-To: Daren J Farmer
X-cc: 
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \Darren_Farmer_Dec2000\Notes Folders\Logistics
X-Origin: Farmer-D
X-FileName: dfarmer.nsf

Subject: King Ranch Gas Plant- 12/2000 Election

HPL has elected to be kept whole with respect to processing during the month 
of December 2000 on its gas delivered from the Three Rivers Gathering 
System.  There should be no reduction for shrinkage and fuel at the plant for 
December 2000.


HPL will be kept whole with respect to ethane recoveries from the Big Cowboy 
gas being processed at the King Ranch Gas Plant during the month of December 
2000.  This election will reduce the shrinkage percentage from 20% of the 
inlet MMBtu's to 15% of the inlet MMBtu's.

If you have any questions please give me a call.

Thanks!

Blanca
